name: We-Math
intro: We-Math是一个旨在评估大型多模态模型（LMMs）视觉数学推理能力的基准。它超越了传统的端到端性能评估，深入探究模型在知识获取和泛化方面的潜在原理。该基准包含6.5K个视觉数学问题，涵盖67个分层知识概念和五层知识粒度。We-Math引入了四维指标（IK、IG、CM、RM），以分层评估LMMs推理过程中的固有问题。
org: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
metric: Insufficient Knowledge (IK), Inadequate Generalization (IG), Complete Mastery (CM), Rote Memorizatio
intro_en: We-Math is a benchmark designed to evaluate the visual mathematical reasoning abilities of large multimodal models (LMMs). It goes beyond traditional end-to-end performance assessment to explore the underlying principles of models' knowledge acquisition and generalization. The benchmark includes 6.5K visual math problems covering 67 hierarchical knowledge concepts across five levels of knowledge granularity. We-Math introduces four-dimensional metrics (IK, IG, CM, RM) to hierarchically assess inherent issues in LMMs' reasoning processes.
metric_en: Insufficient Knowledge (IK), Inadequate Generalization (IG), Complete Mastery (CM), Rote Memorizatio

drawio_review_note: Aligned with We-Math arXiv:2407.01284, Sections 2.1 and 2.2, Section 3, and Appendices B.4-B.5; official repository https://github.com/We-Math/We-Math.. We-Math constructs a five-layer textbook-derived knowledge taxonomy with 99 nodes and 67 terminal concepts, then collects 6,524 new visual multiple-choice math problems from authoritative public sites, exams, and exercises. Eligible items are multi-concept or decomposable, image-question consistent, and have one correct answer with plausible distractors. Three experts label concepts and retain an item only when at least two agree; solution steps and step counts are annotated, and a second expert review checks the diagram, answer, and concept alignment. Composite items are decomposed into coherent concept-specific subproblems. Official scoring uses the 1,740-item Testmini split (1,215 one-step, 360 two-step, and 165 three-step), not the full 6,524-item pool. Evaluation standardizes multiple-choice output, parses it with regular expressions, classifies composite/subproblem correctness into IK, IG, CM, and RM, and reports Score_average = αS_IK + βS_IG + S_CM with default α=0 and β=0.5.
